misconceptions.description: Treating praise such as 'Great start!' as feedback that drives design revision
misconceptions.trigger: feedback line carries tone or encouragement but names no criterion, location, or action
misconceptions.feedback: Rewrite each line as criterion then location then action so the student knows what to change and where.

misconceptions.description: Using directives like 'tighten this up' that never point to a part of the draft
misconceptions.trigger: comment tells the student to improve but does not locate the issue in the draft
misconceptions.feedback: Name the exact frame or element and the observable next move, not a general instruction to improve.

misconceptions.description: Stacking many equal-weight comments so the student cannot tell what to fix first
misconceptions.trigger: template lists multiple revisions with no priority order
misconceptions.feedback: Cap the template at one prioritized revision so the feedback itself does not overload the learner.
